source: made up: exhausted medical resident on a rare golden Sunday off trying to do everything and rest
persona: Dr. Ananya Rao, a PGY-2 internal medicine resident on a rare 'golden weekend' Sunday off after a brutal 75-hour inpatient week. Starts the morning ambitiously trying to cram a week's worth of errands, chart completion, exercise, and cooking into one day, then hits a wall mid-afternoon and asks the app to pare the plan down so she can actually rest.
situation: Sunday morning waking at 09:00 without a pager. Has 6 overdue clinic discharge summaries to sign in Epic, an empty fridge, a mountain of laundry, a friend's afternoon coffee invite, and deep cumulative fatigue.
life: 09:10 Wake up and text the app: golden Sunday off!! I have so much to catch up on—help me schedule: coffee & pancakes, finish 6 overdue Epic discharge summaries, peloton ride + shower, Trader Joe's grocery haul, meal-prep chicken tikka and roasted cauliflower for my 6 AM wards week, wash 2 loads of scrubs/linens, meet my co-resident Priya for coffee at 15:00, and call my parents.
09:15 Remind the app to get the 6 Epic discharge summaries out of the way before noon so hospital medical records stops emailing me.
09:20 Make cardamom coffee and protein pancakes, eating slowly on the couch until 10:15.
10:18 Report coffee and pancakes done. Starting first load of scrubs in the washer and opening my hospital laptop for the 6 Epic discharge summaries.
10:20 Dictate and sign all 6 overdue discharge summaries and clear inbox lab results until 11:55.
11:58 Text the app: Epic charts are 100% zeroed out!! Moved load #1 to the dryer and started load #2. Going to hop on the Peloton for a 30-min ride and shower before Trader Joe's.
12:05 Get 10 minutes into the Peloton warmup and realize your legs feel like lead bricks. Stop at 12:20, take a warm shower, and eat leftover rice and dal until 13:15.
13:18 Text the app: bailed on the Peloton ride after 10 mins, my body is way more wiped from wards than I thought. Showered and ate lunch. Driving to Trader Joe's now so I have food for the week.
13:25 Drive to Trader Joe's; Sunday afternoon crowds are packed, taking until 14:40 to get back and carry four heavy bags upstairs.

14:42 Text the app while putting cold groceries away: just got back from TJ's and I'm honestly hitting a wall. Texting Priya now to ask if we can do a 20-minute phone catch-up instead of me driving across town for 15:00 coffee, and I need a 90-minute nap after that. Please pare down the rest of my afternoon so I only do the essentials (nap, call parents, and meal-prep the chicken tikka for work).
14:55 Put groceries away and chat with co-resident Priya on the phone for 20 minutes while lying on the bed until 15:15.
15:18 Report groceries unpacked and had a nice phone catch-up with Priya instead of driving out. Going to sleep from 15:20 to 16:50.
16:55 Wake up feeling much better. Text the app: nap saved my life. Calling my parents on FaceTime while I fold the two loads of clean scrubs.
17:00 FaceTime parents for 45 minutes while folding scrubs and setting out five pairs for Monday–Friday wards.
17:48 Report parents call and laundry folding done! Starting the big batch of chicken tikka, rice, and roasted cauliflower for the week's hospital lunches and tonight's dinner.
17:50 Cook chicken tikka and roast cauliflower, pack four glass lunch containers for the hospital fridge, and eat dinner until 19:30.
19:35 Report meal prep and dinner done! Pack hospital badge and stethoscope into backpack and read in bed before 21:30 lights out.
constraints: Overdue Epic discharge summaries must be signed before noon so the rest of the day off isn't shadowed by hospital chart reminders.
Meal-prepping weekday hospital lunches and washing scrubs are non-negotiable before Monday's 06:00 inpatient shift.
When cumulative residency fatigue hits mid-day, optional driving/exercise must give way to a 90-minute recovery nap.

truth.item: Start laundry & sign 6 Epic discharge summaries
Short aborted Peloton warmup, shower & lunch
Unpack groceries & phone catch-up with Priya
Call parents & fold 2 loads of scrubs

profile.Work: Internal medicine resident (PGY-2); starts Monday inpatient wards at 06:00.
